media: Below is a video of someone playing it.
first_impression: Charming pastoral aesthetic right out of the gate - feels like A Short Hike blended with an old-school herding arcade loop. But within two minutes you realize half the game is just jogging across empty grass, and sheep pathfinding gets maddeningly sticky at choke points.
best_things: The wolf snatch picture-in-picture window and frantic rescue countdown inject genuine urgency into an otherwise sleepy herding loop.
The herding influence ring is exceptionally readable, giving you instant visual feedback on how creeping shrinks your pressure radius.
The golden-hour low-poly lighting creates a cozy, relaxing countryside vibe that looks great in stills.

worst_problems.problem: Sheep cluster and refuse to cross narrow bottlenecks like the bridge, freezing in place while you awkwardly nudge them from behind.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give sheep a funneling flock AI across bridges and gates so they naturally single-file forward instead of bouncing off invisible barrier angles.

worst_problems.problem: Excessive dead downtime spent holding sprint across empty fields and tree groves with zero interaction or hazards.
worst_problems.suggestion: Condense map scale, add whistle mechanics to call distant sheep, or sprinkle pickups/shortcuts to keep travel engaging.

worst_problems.problem: No visible progression or unlock loop after achieving a 3-star rating, leaving no motivation to play again beyond repeating preset difficulties.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add unlockable maps, farm cosmetics, whistles, or dog customizations earned through stars.

worst_problems.problem: Cluttered text banners and popups repeatedly obstruct the upper and lower screen during tense moments.
worst_problems.suggestion: Fade tutorial tooltips permanently after the first minute and consolidate wolf alerts into subtle world-space audio/visual cues.

worst_problems.problem: Pip's turning and locomotion feel floaty with noticeable foot-sliding during pivots.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add subtle banking on turns, turn-in-place animations, and small ground dust puffs to give the collie tangible weight.

boredom_points: Jogging solo across the pine forest between 00:50 and 02:00 before wolves spawn, with literally nothing happening on screen.
Repeating the exact same fetch-and-deposit pattern three consecutive times on a map with no layout variation.
confusions: Why the sheep panicked and stopped right at the bridge mouth around 03:25 despite having a clear path straight ahead.
Whether the stars on the victory screen unlock new levels or are strictly high-score tracking.
wish_list: Multiple distinct maps (steep cliffs, bogs, coastal farms) with unique environmental hazards.
Whistle commands to herd or hold sheep remotely without running behind every single straggler.
Unlockable dog coats, collies, or stamina perks to give runs a sense of long-term reward.
one_line_review: A gorgeous, cozy herding concept with tense wolf encounters that currently feels more like a 10-minute game jam prototype than a complete purchase.
